### Reasoning
No changes requested, so this preserves the existing FlexibleGate_Def.xml setup. It is a 2D water case because pointmin.y and pointmax.y are both 0, while drawn objects span a thin symmetric y-thickness. Geometry, gate segmentation, and main physical settings were copied directly from the provided case. Parameters reflect the original Newtonian water setup with Chrono-coupled floating gate blocks.

### Geometry XML
```xml
<geometry>
    <definition dp="0.01" units_comment="metres (m)">
        <pointmin x="-0.1" y="0" z="-0.1" />
        <pointmax x="2.1" y="0" z="1.1" />
    </definition>
    <commands>
        <list name="GateBlock" printcall="false">
            <drawbox>
                <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
                <point x="0.5" y="-0.1" z="0" />
                <size x="0.03" y="0.2" z="0.2" />
            </drawbox>
            <move x="0" y="0" z="0.2" />
            <setmknextbound next="true" />
        </list>
        <list name="GateBlockSmall" printcall="false">
            <drawbox>
                <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
                <point x="0.5" y="-0.1" z="0" />
                <size x="0.03" y="0.2" z="0.15" />
            </drawbox>
            <move x="0" y="0" z="0.15" />
            <setmknextbound next="true" />
        </list>
        <mainlist>
            <setshapemode>real | bound</setshapemode>
            <setdrawmode mode="full" />
            <setmkfluid mk="0" />
            <drawbox>
                <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
                <point x="0" y="-0.1" z="0" />
                <size x="0.5" y="0.2" z="0.6" />
            </drawbox>
            <drawbox>
                <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
                <point x="0" y="-0.1" z="0" />
                <size x="2.0" y="0.2" z="0.05" />
            </drawbox>
            <setmkbound mk="0" />
            <drawbox>
                <boxfill>all^top</boxfill>
                <point x="0" y="-0.1" z="0" />
                <size x="2.0" y="0.2" z="1.2" />
            </drawbox>
            <shapeout file="Domain" />
            <setmkbound mk="1" />
            <move x="0" y="0" z="0.05" />
            <runlist name="GateBlockSmall" />
            <runlist name="GateBlock" times="4" />
            <matrixreset />
            <shapeout file="Gate" />
        </mainlist>
    </commands>
</geometry>
```

- I identified the likely flexible gate as boundary `Mk = 15` based on its tall, slender geometry.
- The overlaid curves are for 6 selected times spanning the simulation.

If you want, I can also:
1. plot more specific times you choose,
2. isolate a different gate segment (`Mk = 11–15` seem to be stacked vertical sections),
3. or make a cleaner figure with all gate segments combined into one full gate outline.
What is the net force applied by the fluid onto the flexible gate over time?

I computed the net fluid force on the flexible gate by summing the fluid-force histories for gate segments `mk = 11–15`.

Saved outputs:
- `out/analysis/ForcesGate_net_over_time.png`
- `out/analysis/ForcesGate_net_from_segments.csv`
- `out/analysis/ForcesGate_net_summary.txt`

Key result:
- Maximum net fluid force magnitude: `720.87 N/m`
- Time of maximum: `2.00 s`

Force components at that time:
- `Fx = 718.75 N/m`
- `Fy ≈ 0`
- `Fz = 55.29 N/m`

Important note:
- `ComputeForces` reported units of `N/m`, not `N`, so this is force per unit width, consistent with a 2D-style setup or extrusion interpretation.

Also, the combined `ForcesGateAll.csv` command failed, so I used the reliable approach of summing the individual segment files.

If you want, I can next:
1. break down which gate segment carries the most load over time,
2. plot only the horizontal force `Fx`,
3. or compute impulse by integrating force over time.
